activity_context.topic_title: Sums of Finite Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation

feedback.problem: Determine the value of the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{4}\frac{1}{{6}^{n}}$  rounded to $3$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the series as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}\frac{1}{{6}^{n}}={\sum }_{n=1}^{4}{(\frac{1}{6})}^{n}
$$

Since the above series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=\frac{1}{6}$ and $N=4.$ We need to figure out ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}={(\frac{1}{6})}^{n},
$$

and therefore the first term of the series is

$$
{a}_{1}={(\frac{1}{6})}^{1}=\frac{1}{6}.
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=\frac{1}{6},r=\frac{1}{6}$ and $N=4$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}{(\frac{1}{6})}^{n} & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{6})}^{4}]}{(1-\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [1-{(\frac{1}{6})}^{4}] \\  & ≈0.200\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the final answer has been rounded to three decimal places.
